description: Authorization patterns including RBAC, ABAC, permission management, and Spring Security authorization

questions.question: What is the difference between RBAC and ABAC?
questions.answer: RBAC (Role-Based Access Control): Access based on user roles. User assigned roles (Admin, Manager, User), roles have permissions. Simple, widely used. Example: Admin role can delete users, Manager can view reports, User can view own data. ABAC (Attribute-Based Access Control): Access based on attributes (user, resource, environment). More flexible, fine-grained. Example: Allow if user.department == resource.department AND time.hour < 18 AND request.location == 'office'. RBAC: User 'john' has role 'Manager' → can approve expenses. ABAC: User 'john' can approve expenses if expense.amount < 5000 AND expense.department == john.department AND john.level >= 'senior'. RBAC simpler for static permissions, ABAC better for complex, dynamic rules. Spring Security supports both. Use RBAC for: simple hierarchy, stable roles. Use ABAC for: context-dependent access, many permission combinations.
